clue.text: Ponder rise in total energy

indicators.note: in a down clue a rise reads the word upwards, so the total is written backwards

parts.note: a total is a sum
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Someone considers a sudden jump in total energy consumption.
explanation.definitionFit: To muse is to think something over at leisure, a synonym of ponder.

clue.text: Isotope has decayed, achieving final state

indicators.note: a decayed isotope has broken down, so these letters break down and re-form

explanation.surface: A radioactive isotope decays until it reaches its stable end product.
explanation.walkthrough: 'decayed' rearranges ISOTOPE HAS; 'achieving' just links wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An apotheosis is the culmination or highest point, the ultimate stage something reaches.

clue.text: King and Queen worried about a martial activity

indicators.note: the royal pair and their worry sit about the single letter, wrapping round it

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king
R, for Regina, is the standard abbreviation for a queen
ate, as in 'what's eating you?', means worried

explanation.surface: A royal couple fret over some warlike pursuit.
explanation.definitionFit: Karate is a Japanese martial art, so an example of a combat discipline.

clue.text: Director in part picked up business in rich area

indicators.note: in a down clue, picking something up lifts it so it reads bottom to top
the director's letter goes in among the letters of the part

parts.note: an actor's part is a role
ado is fuss or business, as in 'without further ado'

explanation.surface: A film director who took a role found a lucrative line of work in a wealthy district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'picked up' looks like a homophone signal, but in a down clue it lifts RODLE so it reads ELDOR.
explanation.definitionFit: El Dorado was the legendary city of gold, now any place of fabulous wealth or opportunity.

clue.text: Has debt, large, covering our group

indicators.note: the size letters cover, i.e. surround, the group pronoun

parts.note: OS stands for outsize, a clothing label for large
we is the pronoun for a group including the speaker

explanation.surface: A borrower has a big debt that covers everyone in the family.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who owes is in debt to another, the verb form of having a debt.

clue.text: Irish party suppressing new fad, left-wing and philistine

indicators.note: the party letters hold down, so enclose, the next pieces

parts.note: UU is the Ulster Unionists, a Northern Irish political party
a cult is a passing craze or fad
red is the colour of the political left

explanation.surface: A Northern Irish party clamps down on a trendy new craze, and is called leftist and boorish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suppressing' is the container signal: the party holds down what follows. 'Irish party' is the Ulster Unionists of Northern Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: A philistine is indifferent or hostile to the arts, which is to say lacking in culture.

clue.text: Philosopher's name enshrined by revolutionary generation

indicators.note: revolving the hidden letters turns them round, so they read backwards
the philosopher's name lies enclosed within the letters of the next word

explanation.surface: A thinker's name is honoured by a radical generation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'enshrined by' finds ENER in 'generation'; 'revolutionary' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: René Descartes, the French philosopher, had René as his first name.

clue.text: Take place of our team, getting promoted around end of year

parts.note: us is the side we belong to

indicators.note: the word for promoted wraps round the final letter of the year

parts.note: someone promoted has gone up

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: Our club displaces a rival, winning promotion as the season ends.
explanation.definitionFit: To usurp is to seize another's position wrongfully, i.e. to supplant them.

clue.text: Anvil user hammered without exception

indicators.note: metal hammered on an anvil is reshaped, so these letters are beaten into a new order

explanation.surface: A blacksmith using an anvil pounded away at everything.
explanation.definitionFit: Universal means applying to all cases, so true without exception.

clue.text: Grant a couple of pounds in the past, to go round Perth area

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for a pound (libra), so two of them

indicators.note: the word for formerly goes round the abbreviation for the region

parts.note: once means at some former time
WA is Western Australia, the state whose capital is Perth

explanation.surface: Someone was once given a small sum to travel around the Perth region.
explanation.walkthrough: Perth here is the Australian city, not the Scottish one.
explanation.definitionFit: An allowance is a sum granted regularly, so a grant in the noun sense.

clue.text: Difficulty in moving train i.e. after wreck

indicators.note: after a crash a train's carriages are jumbled, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A train struggles to get going after a crash, that is.
explanation.definitionFit: Inertia is resistance to motion, the tendency of a body to stay at rest.

clue.text: Unusual rocky material enthralling science graduate attending university

indicators.note: enthralling holds captive, so the mineral's letters hold the others inside

parts.note: ore is rock from which metal is extracted
a BSc is a Bachelor of Science degree

explanation.surface: An odd mineral fascinates a science graduate at university.
explanation.definitionFit: Something obscure is little known, so out of the ordinary or unusual.

clue.text: Expected back around ten initially — English study

indicators.note: the reversed word goes round the initial of ten
back means the word for expected is read in reverse

parts.note: something due is expected, as a train due at noon

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: An English study was due back about ten.
explanation.definitionFit: An étude is a musical study, a piece written to practise a technique.

clue.text: Not welcoming one nursed by worried nun — coming to call is cancelled

indicators.note: a nursed thing is held in the arms, so the shuffled nun encloses the numeral
worried means agitated, so these letters are stirred up

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: cancelled means the little word is struck out of the visit word

parts.note: visiting is coming to call on someone

explanation.surface: A nervous nun tends someone, while her visit is called off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worried' rearranges NUN to UNN; 'cancelled' strikes IS from VISITING, leaving VITING.
explanation.definitionFit: Uninviting means unattractive or off-putting, the reverse of a friendly welcome.

clue.text: A lot of additional material arrived back, offering little substance

indicators.note: back means the whole run of letters is read in reverse
a lot of means most of the word, so its last letter goes

parts.note: detail is extra, supplementary material
came means arrived

explanation.surface: A report notes that most of the extra content came back, offering little of substance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A lot of' drops L from DETAIL; 'back' turns DETAICAME around.
explanation.definitionFit: An emaciated body is abnormally thin, with little flesh or bulk to it.

clue.text: Exclusive group — I left organisation of alumni getting it set up

indicators.note: organisation arranges, so these letters are put into a new order
in a down clue set up raises the word so it reads upwards

explanation.surface: Someone leaves the alumni association as it is getting established.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organisation of' rearranges ALUMNI to LUMINA; 'set up' turns IT to TI.
explanation.definitionFit: The Illuminati were a secret society, the name now used for any supposedly elite circle.

clue.text: Face Conservative in most recent uprising regarding speech

parts.note: a clock's dial is its face

indicators.note: in a down clue an uprising lifts the letters so they read upwards
the party letter goes inside the word for recent

parts.note: late can mean most recent, as in 'her late novel'

explanation.surface: A politician confronts a Tory in a recent revolt over a speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Dialectal relates to dialect, a regional variety of language, so it concerns the way people talk.

clue.text: European people, very smart, though changing at the end

indicators.note: the final letter of the word for smart is swapped for another

parts.note: swish means very smart or fashionable

explanation.surface: Some European nationals are very stylish, though they change at the end.
explanation.walkthrough: The last letter of SWISH changes from H to S.
explanation.definitionFit: The Swiss are the people of Switzerland, a central European nation.

clue.text: Letter from Greece slipped into our house

indicators.note: the answer has slipped into the following words and lies within them

explanation.surface: A letter posted from Greece was pushed through our door.
explanation.definitionFit: Rho is the seventeenth letter of the Greek alphabet, written like a P.

clue.text: Unduly force bar staff to welcome one

parts.note: a rail is a bar

indicators.note: the staff takes in, i.e. welcomes, the letter for one

parts.note: a rod is a staff or stick
a means one, as in 'a dog'

explanation.surface: A manager pressures the bar staff into greeting a newcomer.
explanation.definitionFit: To railroad is to push someone or something through hastily, coercing them.

clue.text: Poet runs into pub, expressing final line

indicators.note: the cricket letter goes into the shortened pub word
expressing squeezes out, so the final occurrence is pressed out of the word

parts.note: a local is a British drinker's regular neighbourhood pub
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A poet dashes into a pub, voicing his last line.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'local' is a British drinker's nearest pub. 'expressing final' squeezes the last L out of LOCAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Federico García Lorca was a celebrated Spanish poet and playwright.

clue.text: Showering and seducing, leading with the other hand

indicators.note: the leading letter, R for right, is replaced by the other hand, L for left

parts.note: ravishing can mean enrapturing or seducing

explanation.surface: A boxer showers and dazzles opponents by leading with the weaker hand.
explanation.walkthrough: R (right) at the front of RAVISHING becomes L (left).
explanation.definitionFit: Lavishing means heaping or pouring generously, so bestowing in abundance as if in a shower.

clue.text: Dull time turning over small space in yard?

indicators.note: in a down clue turning over flips the letters so they read upwards

parts.note: a drag is a tedious time
an en is a small typographical space, half an em

explanation.surface: A boring spell is spent digging over a little patch of the yard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'yard?' reads as part of the surface, but it is the definition: GARDEN is American for yard, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: In American usage the yard is the plot round a house, called a garden in Britain.

clue.text: F, say, for 'flying insect'

parts.note: read as wordplay the answer splits into mid, G and E: F stands midway between G and E in the alphabet

explanation.surface: A grade F is given out for a piece about a flying insect.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: the answer, broken up, describes the clue. F sits midway between E and G.
explanation.definitionFit: A midge is a tiny flying insect, often seen in biting swarms.

clue.text: Number in computer support, for instance, having little hesitation providing mathematical quantity

indicators.note: the number letter is placed in the computer abbreviation

parts.note: IT, information technology, is the computer support department
e.g. is the abbreviation for 'for example'
er is a short sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: Someone working in computer support hesitates briefly before supplying a figure.
explanation.definitionFit: An integer is a whole number, one kind of mathematical quantity.

clue.text: European country investing in oil mostly upset Nigerian people

indicators.note: investing in means putting money into, so the country goes inside
in a down clue upset turns the letters upside down so they read upwards
mostly means all but the last letter

parts.note: GB is the abbreviation for Great Britain

explanation.surface: A European nation pours money into oil, mostly upsetting the local Nigerians.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' trims OIL to OI; 'upset' turns that to IO.
explanation.definitionFit: The Igbo are a major ethnic group of south-eastern Nigeria.

clue.text: Bring up Government dispute

parts.note: a row is a quarrel or dispute

explanation.surface: Someone raises a government quarrel.
explanation.definitionFit: To grow crops or plants is to raise or cultivate them, a sense of bring up.

clue.text: Asian currency cartel linked to awkward customer?

parts.note: a ring is a group colluding to control prices, like a cartel
git is British slang for a contemptible or awkward person

explanation.surface: A price-fixing currency cartel is in league with a difficult client.
explanation.definitionFit: The ringgit is the monetary unit of Malaysia, so it is Asian money.

clue.text: Sentimentality and a dash of dreaminess can be excellent

parts.note: goo is sickly sentimentality

indicators.note: a dash is a tiny amount, so only the first letter of the word is used

explanation.surface: A little schmaltz and dreaminess can make a fine film.
explanation.definitionFit: Good and excellent are near synonyms of high quality.

clue.text: Nice show of friendliness, encouraging you to go!

definitions.text: Nice show of friendliness, encouraging you to go!

parts.words: Nice show of friendliness, encouraging you to go!
parts.note: Nice is the French city, so the friendly send-off is in French

explanation.surface: A pleasant gesture that politely urges you to leave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nice' looks like an adjective, but capitalised it is the French city, signalling a French phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase wishes a departing traveller a pleasant journey, a friendly farewell.

clue.text: Cost to be paid when hosting Republican internet pest

indicators.note: the fee word hosts, so holds inside, the party letter

parts.note: a toll is a charge paid for use of a road or bridge

explanation.surface: A fee is levied on Republicans hosting an online nuisance.
explanation.definitionFit: A troll posts provocative messages online to upset others, a nuisance on the web.
